questions.question: What does TTFT measure in LLM serving?
options: Time from request receipt to the last output token
Time from request receipt to the first output token (prefill + queue + network)
Time between consecutive output tokens during decode
Total tokens processed per second across the fleet
questions.explanation: TTFT (Time to First Token) measures the elapsed time from when a request is received to when the first output token is generated. It encompasses prefill time, queue wait, and network round-trip.

questions.question: What is goodput and why does the lesson call it the metric that actually matters for product?
options: Total tokens per second — the headline throughput figure providers advertise
The fraction of requests that met every SLO constraint simultaneously (TTFT, TPOT, E2E)
The ratio of successful requests to failed requests over a time window
Tokens generated minus tokens that caused refusals or errors
questions.explanation: Goodput is the fraction of requests that met all SLO constraints simultaneously. High throughput at low goodput means you are processing tokens that never reach users on time — the product is broken even if the GPU is busy.

questions.question: For Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on TRT-LLM in 2026, what are the reference mean TTFT and mean TPOT values?
options: TTFT: 50 ms, TPOT: 2 ms
TTFT: 162 ms, TPOT: 7.33 ms
TTFT: 500 ms, TPOT: 20 ms
TTFT: 1,093 ms, TPOT: 50 ms
questions.explanation: The lesson provides reference numbers: mean TTFT 162 ms, mean TPOT 7.33 ms, mean E2E 1,093 ms for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on TRT-LLM in 2026. These are production-calibrated baselines to compare against.

questions.question: NVIDIA GenAI-Perf and LLMPerf measure TPOT differently for the same run. What is the key difference?
options: GenAI-Perf uses wall-clock time while LLMPerf uses GPU-time
GenAI-Perf excludes TTFT from the ITL calculation (starts from token 2); LLMPerf includes TTFT (starts from token 1)
GenAI-Perf measures TPOT in milliseconds while LLMPerf uses microseconds
GenAI-Perf averages over all requests while LLMPerf reports the median
questions.explanation: This is the measurement trap: GenAI-Perf excludes TTFT from the ITL calculation (inter-token latency starts at token 2), while LLMPerf includes TTFT (starts at token 1). Two tools benchmarking the same system will report different TPOT numbers.

questions.question: Why should you always report P50/P90/P99 rather than mean for LLM serving metrics?
options: Percentiles are required by OpenTelemetry's metric specification
Mean hides the long tail — users experiencing P99 latency have a broken experience even if mean looks fine
LLM outputs are non-deterministic so means are statistically meaningless
P99 is the standard metric in SLO contracts and easier to defend to customers
questions.explanation: LLM latency distributions are heavy-tailed. Mean TTFT of 162 ms masks a P99 that could be 1,000 ms+. Users at the tail have a broken experience. Percentiles reveal the shape; mean conceals it.

questions.question: A team sets an SLO of TTFT P99 <= 800 ms AND TPOT P99 <= 25 ms AND E2E P99 <= 3 s. During a load test, 98% of requests meet all three constraints. What is the goodput?
options: Cannot be determined from this information
questions.explanation: Goodput is the fraction of requests meeting all SLO constraints simultaneously. If 98% of requests satisfy all three constraints at once, goodput is 98% — regardless of how each individual metric performs in isolation.
